subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default proactive retention policy for stale session archive artifacts beyond the existing deleted/reset retention, store-temp cleanup, unreferenced-artifact sweep, and disk-budget paths?
rationale: The source shows real partial cleanup, but broad automatic deletion of session archives affects retention, diagnostics, and recovery semantics, and an open PR already covers the narrower deleted/reset reporting gap.

options.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
options.body: Define which `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.tmp`, `.bak.*`, checkpoint, and trajectory artifacts are automatically removed, under which retention and mode rules.

options.title: Land Narrow Reporting First
options.body: Treat the open PR as the immediate fix for deleted/reset visibility and defer proactive `.bak.*` and broader suffix cleanup until more production evidence lands.

options.title: Split By Artifact Class
options.body: Keep this broad report as a parent and route each remaining suffix or sidecar class to a narrower canonical issue with its own safety proof.

recommendation.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
recommendation.body: Define which `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.tmp`, `.bak.*`, checkpoint, and trajectory artifacts are automatically removed, under which retention and mode rules.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision extends the cleanup and maintenance policy surface introduced in the session/cron maintenance hardening work.
